QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_43

question.text: The collateral deposited as Base Minimum Capital must satisfy which composition requirement?

answer.text: At least 50% must be in the form of cash or cash equivalents (including fixed deposits and bank guarantees)
At least 75% must be in government securities
No composition requirement exists; any form of collateral is acceptable

explanation.text: The Logic: The clearing corporation requires that at least 50% of the BMC must be in the form of cash or cash equivalents (which includes fixed deposits and bank guarantees). The remaining 50% can be in the form of approved non-cash collateral such as government securities or equity shares (with appropriate haircuts). The Trap: It is not 100% cash. There IS a composition requirement. The cash/cash-equivalent component has a minimum threshold. Cross-Exam Context: Collateral composition rules are part of the risk management framework. Distributor's Pro-Tip: BMC composition: minimum 50% in cash/cash equivalents. Balance in approved collateral with haircuts.
